questions.stem: What are ACID and BaSE, and how do they relate to each other?
options: Two file formats used in Hadoop
Two query languages for NoSQL databases
Two stages of the same transaction
Two data consistency models that compete on a use-case basis
Two types of database index
questions.explanation: ACID and BaSE are both data consistency models, chosen according to the requirements of the use case.

options: Backup, Security and Encryption
Basically Available, Soft State and Eventually Consistent
Batch, Stream and Event processing
Balanced, Sharded and Elastic
Basic Access, Standard Enforcement
questions.explanation: BaSE is about Basically Available, Soft State and Eventually Consistent.

questions.stem: What is the basic difference between what the ACID model and the BaSE model provide?
options: ACID provides speed; BaSE provides security
ACID provides storage; BaSE provides compute
ACID provides availability; BaSE provides consistency
ACID provides encryption; BaSE provides compression
ACID provides a consistent system; BaSE provides high availability
questions.explanation: The ACID model provides a consistent system, whereas the BaSE model provides high availability.

questions.stem: What does "Basically Available" mean in the BaSE model?
options: The system is guaranteed to be available in the event of failure
The system is available only during business hours
The system is available only for reads
The system guarantees immediate consistency
The system is available on a single node only
questions.explanation: Basically Available means the system is guaranteed to remain available even when failures occur.

questions.stem: What does "Soft State" mean in the BaSE model?
options: Data is stored in memory rather than on disk
Data is deleted after a fixed time
Data values may change over time because immediate consistency is not enforced, with responsibility for consistency delegated to developers
The schema of the data can change without notice
Only part of the data is written on each operation
questions.explanation: Because BaSE lacks immediate consistency, values may change over time; the database no longer enforces consistency and leaves that to developers.

questions.stem: What does "Eventually Consistent" imply about reading data before consistency has been achieved?
options: Reads are blocked until the data is consistent
Reads return an error
Reads are still possible, although they might not reflect reality
Reads are served from a backup
Reads are only allowed on the primary node
questions.explanation: BaSE does eventually achieve consistency, but until then reads remain possible even though they may not reflect the true current state.

questions.stem: For which kind of system is the ACID model described as a must?
options: OLTP systems, such as banking, where users cannot afford an inconsistent database
Marketing and campaigning systems built on semi-structured data
Social media feeds
Data lakes on object storage
Log analytics platforms
questions.explanation: ACID is essential for OLTP systems like banking, where a deposit must be recorded before a withdrawal can proceed.

questions.stem: Which category of databases mostly supports the BaSE model?
options: RDBMS databases
Mainframe databases
OLTP banking databases
Spreadsheet-based databases
NoSQL databases
questions.explanation: Most SQL/RDBMS databases support ACID, whereas most NoSQL databases support the BaSE model.

questions.stem: Which use case is given as one that can live without ACID features?
options: Bank withdrawals
Marketing and campaigning on huge semi-structured or unstructured datasets
Payroll processing
Stock trading
Airline seat reservations
questions.explanation: Marketing and campaigning workloads focus on huge datasets from everywhere and can tolerate a loss of consistency, unlike OLTP systems.

questions.stem: Hadoop and Object Storage are not ACID compliant. Which product is named as providing an ACID model on top of Object Storage?
options: Hive
HDFS
MapReduce
Delta Lake from Databricks
YARN
questions.explanation: Databricks, through its Delta Lake product, provides an ACID model on top of Object Storage.
